questions.question: In the Narmada Payments audit after 120 turns, what filled most of the context?
options: The system prompt and tool definitions
questions.explanation: Old raw CSV extracts took about 410,000 tokens, most of it stale.

questions.question: Why does just-in-time loading usually win for long sessions?
options: It removes the need for tools
It makes the system prompt longer
The agent gets lightweight references and fetches detail only when needed, avoiding context bloat
questions.explanation: Just-in-time loading keeps context small; its trade-off is extra round trips, which matter little in long sessions.

questions.question: What is the critical implementation detail when using compaction?
options: Append only the text of each response
Append the full response.content to your history each turn
questions.explanation: Dropping non-text blocks loses the compaction state, so keep all of response.content.

questions.question: Where should details that must survive exactly, like account numbers or agreed decisions, be kept?
options: In external memory such as a progress file
In the hope a summary keeps them
In the system prompt, edited each turn
questions.explanation: Summaries are lossy, so critical facts belong in external memory the agent writes and reads.
